title: Feed refresh job discards fetched feed data instead of refreshing persisted state

evidence.quote: BGAppRefreshTask for Feed Pre-Fetching ... Keep RSS feed content fresh so digest generation is fast
Fetch only top N feeds per run ... Store "last refreshed" / "next due" per feed
let feeds = try await self.feedRepository.getEnabledFeeds() ... _ = try await feedParser.parseFeed(url: feed.url, feedName: feed.name)

reasoning: The feed refresh handler fetches enabled feeds and parses each feed, but the parse result is assigned to _ and there is no call to update feed lastFetched, cache raw articles, or otherwise persist the work. The later local digest path builds a fresh ArticleRepository and fetches/processes feeds again, so this background job appears to consume the BGAppRefresh budget without making foreground or overnight generation fresher or faster. Confidence is medium because EpilogueFeedParser could have hidden side effects, but no included evidence shows any persisted cache or repository update.
reproduction: Run handleFeedRefreshTask with enabled feeds, then inspect feedRepository state or run a subsequent digest generation. The handler has no write path from parsed results to repositories, so the subsequent generation still has to fetch/process feeds normally.
recommendation: Route feed refresh through the same caching/persistence layer the digest generator will read, or remove/rename the job if it is only a connectivity warm-up. At minimum, update lastFetched/nextDue state and store fetched raw articles or HTTP cache metadata so the next digest can reuse the work.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no tests for handleFeedRefreshTask. The parser is constructed directly inside the private handler, which also makes it hard to assert that parsed results are persisted or that repository update methods are called.
suggestedRegressionTest: Introduce injectable feed-refresh dependencies and test that a successful refresh persists refreshed metadata/articles for each fetched feed and that a subsequent digest generation can consume the cached result without refetching the same feed.
minimumFixScope: LocalDigestScheduler feed refresh handler plus the smallest repository/cache API needed to persist refresh output.
